proposals.before: After Murong Bao succeeded, he appointed Murong De as commissioner bearing credentials, area commander-in-chief of military affairs in six provinces Ji, Yan, Qing, Xu, Jing, and Yu, specially advanced, chariot and cavalry general-in-chief, governor of Ji, concurrently colonel of the Southern Man, stationed at Ye, abolished the rear headquarters, and used the area command to oversee the southern summer in full.
proposals.after: After Murong Bao succeeded, he appointed Murong De as commissioner bearing credentials, area commander-in-chief of military affairs in the six provinces Ji, Yan, Qing, Xu, Jing, and Yu, specially advanced, chariot-and-cavalry general-in-chief, governor of Ji, concurrently colonel of the Southern Man, stationed at Ye; he abolished the rear headquarters and used the area command to oversee the southern Xia domains in full.
proposals.reason: 南夏 means the southern Chinese/Xia lands, not “southern summer”; literal mistranslates 夏.

proposals.before: When Chui succeeded the throne, he was changed to Prince of Fanyang, gradually promoted prefect of Wei, with addition of regular attendant for scattered cavalry.
proposals.after: When Chui succeeded the throne, [De] was changed to Prince of Fanyang, gradually promoted to Yin of Wei (capital-region prefect), and given the additional title of Cavalier Regular Attendant.
proposals.reason: Literal omits the silent subject (De) and under-renders 魏尹 (Yin of Wei).

proposals.before: After Murong Chui’s rebellion collapsed he was deported to Chang’an, where Fu Jian named him prefect of Zhangye; a few years later he was sent home in disgrace.
proposals.after: After Murong Chui’s defeat he was moved to Chang’an, where Fu Jian named him prefect of Zhangye; a few years later he was dismissed and sent home.
proposals.reason: Chinese 垂敗 is Chui’s defeat, not specifically “rebellion collapsed”; 免歸 is dismissal and return, not necessarily “disgrace.”

proposals.before: Ding Tong, chief clerk under Tuoba Zhang, defected with his troops and reported that Zhang's army was exhausted and vulnerable.
proposals.after: Ding Jian, chief clerk under Tuoba Zhang, defected with his troops and reported that Zhang's army was exhausted and vulnerable.
proposals.reason: Chinese 丁建 is Ding Jian; the idiomatic wrongly renders him as Ding Tong (丁通), a different person named later in s0078.

proposals.before: Tuoba Zhang's chief clerk Ding Tong led his masses to surrender and said Tuoba Zhang's army was worn and could be defeated.
proposals.after: Tuoba Zhang's chief clerk Ding Jian led his masses to surrender and said Tuoba Zhang's army was worn and could be defeated.

proposals.before: Before long Murong Bao made Murong De chancellor and governor of Ji, with delegated authority over the southern summer.
proposals.after: Before long Murong Bao made Murong De chancellor and governor of Ji, with delegated authority over the southern Xia domains.
proposals.reason: 南夏 means southern Chinese/Xia lands, not summer.

proposals.before: Murong De sent Central Army Murong Fa and Pacification General Murong He to meet them, and the Jin army was routed.
proposals.after: Murong De sent the Central Army commander Murong Fa, the Pacification General Murong He, and others to resist them, and the Jin army was routed.
proposals.reason: Chinese 等 indicates “and others”; also the Chinese name after 撫軍 is corrupted in the packet but context and English identify Murong He.

proposals.before: We should send eloquent men ahead to persuade, then follow with a great army; Bi Lü Hun once betrayed the state's grace and is sure to turn toward civilization.
proposals.after: We should send eloquent men ahead to persuade, then follow with a great army; Pi Lühun (辟閭渾), who once betrayed the state's grace, is sure to turn toward civilization.
proposals.reason: Chinese 避閭渾 is a corruption of the Jin official 辟閭渾 (Pi Lühun / Bi Lü Hun); keep the packet English surface but note the standard form.

proposals.before: In the fourth year he took the imperial title at the southern altar, amnestied the realm, adopted the Jianping era, placed a mobile temple south of the palace, and dispatched envoys to announce the deed.
proposals.after: In the fourth year [of Longan, AD 400] he assumed the imperial title at the southern suburban altar, issued a general amnesty, changed the era name to Jianping, set a traveling ancestral temple south of the palace, and sent envoys with the accession announcement.
proposals.reason: 四年 here is Eastern Jin Longan 4 / the narrative year leading into Jianping; clarifying avoids mistaking it for Jianping year 4.

proposals.before: At that time Huan Xuan's general was about to usurp and killed those who would not attach to him.
proposals.after: At that time Huan Xuan was about to carry out usurpation and killed those who would not attach to him.
proposals.reason: Chinese 桓玄將行篡逆 means Huan Xuan himself was about to usurp; literal wrongly inserts “Huan Xuan's general.”

proposals.before: When news came of Huan Xuan's fall Murong De mobilized then canceled the campaign because of illness.
proposals.after: Soon they heard Huan Xuan was defeated; Murong De made Murong Zhen the vanguard and Murong Zhong supreme commander, assigning twenty thousand foot and five thousand horse with a set departure date, but Murong De fell ill and therefore halted the army.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic over-compresses the appointments of Murong Zhen and Murong Zhong and the force sizes present in the Chinese.

decisions.reason: 南夏 denotes the southern Xia, meaning the southern Chinese domains; translating 夏 as the season 'summer' is nonsensical in this jurisdictional context.
The silent subject remains Murong De, and 魏尹 is the capital-region office Yin of Wei rather than a generic prefecture. The proposal restores both points.
垂敗 says that Chui was defeated; it does not characterize the event as a collapsed rebellion. 免歸 directly states dismissal and return, without the added claim that the return was disgraceful.
The source explicitly names 丁建, Ding Jian. Ding Tong is a different person who appears later in the chapter and should not be substituted here.
The literal field repeats the same confusion of 丁建 with the later Ding Tong. Ding Jian is the only name attested in this sentence.
As in the earlier appointment, 南夏 denotes the southern Xia domains under delegated authority, not 'southern summer.'
The source lists Murong Fa, Murong He, and others (等), and uses 距 in the sense of resisting the Jin force. The proposal restores the omitted collective and clarifies the offices.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 中軍慕容法、撫軍慕容和等距之

decisions.after: We should send eloquent men ahead to persuade them, then follow with a great army; Pilü Hun, who once betrayed the state's grace, is sure to turn toward civilization.
decisions.reason: The official's standard name is 辟閭渾, romanized Pilü Hun: Pilü is the compound surname and Hun the given name. The chapter's 避閭渾 is a textual variant, not a basis for the split and misread 'Bi Lü Hun.'

sourceWitness.citation: jinshu/127 s0131; Hàn Diǎn entry for 辟閭; Jinshu annals parallel

decisions.after: In Long'an 4 (AD 400), he claimed the imperial title at the southern suburban altar, issued a general amnesty, inaugurated the Jianping era, established a traveling ancestral temple south of the palace, and sent envoys bearing the accession proclamation.
decisions.reason: The narrative's fourth year is Long'an 4 (AD 400), when Murong De inaugurated Jianping. The revision preserves the source's disapproving 僭 with 'claimed' and makes the date and accession sequence explicit.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 四年，僭即皇帝位於南郊…改元為建平

decisions.reason: 將行篡逆 takes Huan Xuan as its subject: he was about to usurp. Treating 將 as the noun 'general' invents another actor and corrupts the syntax.

The existing idiomatic sentence drops the named vanguard and commander, the assigned infantry and cavalry, and the fixed departure date. The proposal accurately restores those material details before Murong De's illness halted the expedition.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 以慕容鎮為前鋒，慕容鐘為大都督，配以步卒二萬，騎五千

claimRetractions.reason: This false alias was inferred from the mistranslated English even though both the Chinese and the extraction's primary claim identify Ding Jian.

claimRevisions.reason: The standard form 辟閭渾 has the compound surname Pilü; revise the inferred normalized name without changing its evidentiary status.

sourceWitness.citation: Hàn Diǎn entry for 辟閭; Jinshu annals parallel

claimRevisions.reason: Preserve the chapter's explicit variant graph 避 while normalizing the English and pinyin to the same historical person, Pilü Hun.
